description.p: Co-op arcade games with your friends, online. Coinmates is based on MAME and lets 2 to 4 players beat up, shoot and race through the arcade co-op classics over the internet, without the input lag of classic netplay. It uses rollback, like modern fighting games: your inputs act at once, and when a friend's input arrives late, the last few frames are quietly redone.

ul.li: Also for Windows and Mac, and players on different systems play together
No accounts and no servers to run: the host gets a 7-character room code, and the others type it in
Whoever drops out can join again, and the game goes on meanwhile
Players at home find each other even without internet
Ready to play with a controller or the keyboard

description.p: ROMs are not included: Coinmates looks for them in Emulation/roms/arcade in your home, or on an SD card (the folders of EmuDeck, which isn't needed), and needs the sets of MAME 0.289. 256 co-op games are checked for netplay.

screenshot.caption: Pick a game among the ones you have
Play alone, host a room, or join one
Join with the room code a friend sent you

description.p: The other players measure how late each player's inputs reach them, and the input delay follows that instead of the round trip. Every player needs this version: it can't play with 1.2.0.

ul.li: Room codes have 7 characters, without the hyphen: much harder to guess
When the connection is bad one way only, such as a phone losing packets as it sends, the game stalls far less
On a phone the input delay is lower and steadier
Playing alone, the BIOS can be chosen again; states saved alone with 1.2.0 don't load
Typing the host's address works only from the same local network or through Tailscale
Whoever joins keeps their own DIP switches for playing alone; online the menu doesn't show them
Joining a game already going is refused with a message, when its state is too big to catch up
On a Mac, the room logs are in Library/Logs/Coinmates

description.p: The input delay adapts by itself, during the game, to the connection and to each player's computer: the setting to choose it is gone. Every player needs this version: it can't play with 1.1.0.

ul.li: With friends far away the game no longer slows down: the inputs wait a little more instead
A Steam Deck or a slow computer with a heavy game keeps up: the others delay their inputs just enough
Macs, Intel and Apple silicon, compute the games exactly as Linux and Windows: the math functions are the same everywhere

description.p: Rooms are found through public BitTorrent trackers instead of the DHT, also on mobile data. Every player needs this version: it can't play with 1.0.0.

ul.li: Joining takes a few seconds, between homes and phones too
Rooms of 3 and 4 players get everyone connected to each other
A build for Intel Macs
Hardened Windows builds

description.p: The first release, for Linux, Windows and Mac.

ul.li: Rollback netplay for 2 to 4 players in 256 co-op arcade games
Rooms with a code, found without servers
Whoever leaves can join again during the game
Report a Problem, with the log of the room
